implementationStatus: Design studies only; application components are unchanged.

branding.rule: Only the current website displays the original emblem and complete wordmark, including Sebastian/ and the slash. The sibling website uses ordinary outbound text, never a second logo or an abbreviated lockup.

header.geometry: One inset floating white shell with continuous corners and a diffuse shadow. The current logo, local navigation and language occupy the main area; a small neutral utility capsule at the far end contains an outbound text link.
header.hierarchy: One current-site logo and local controls, followed by a visually secondary outward text destination. The sibling entry has no emblem or wordmark treatment.
header.languageBehavior: The language control belongs to the current site. Cross-site links retain the selected language.

header.cornerTreatment: Smooth continuous iOS-style corners on all four exterior corners.
header.shadow: Subtle diffuse neutral shadow; one shadow for the whole shell.
header.rasterScaleNote: 48 CSS pixels is the implementation target; the generated artwork illustrates hierarchy rather than exact CSS measurements.

surfaces.rule: Achromatic surfaces; no adjacent pink and pale-blue fields.

footer.hierarchy: The current website is the publisher: one substantial complete original logo, local navigation, registered company details, social links and legal baseline.

pageEnding.separation: A quiet shared newsletter passage, an unboxed editorial outward invitation with ample white space, and a substantial inset current-site footer. These areas have different composition, scale and purpose.
pageEnding.siblingOfferRole: An editorial question or invitation, an explanatory sentence, one plain-text outward action and a small supporting illustration. No sibling logo, emblem, wordmark treatment or navigation index.
pageEnding.paletteRule: Neutral surfaces, no pink/pale-blue panels or mixed pastel cards.
pageEnding.dividerRule: White space separates newsletter and invitation; no divider line is needed there.
